searchText: The second cohort of the core dev apprenticeship program is going to be kicking off in the next few weeks. It'll run for four months during which participants will plan and execute a project focused on something in the core protocol realm. This is your opportunity to both help these new people find a worthwhile project **and** to get more eyes and brains working on the *"thing"* that you wish more people were working on. I encourage you to open an issue here: https://github.com/ethereum-cdap/cohort-one It can be as simple as identifying who you are and what you are working on. It could be an idea for a tool that seems useful. Or maybe some data that needs to be gathered and analyzed. Even things as ambitious as getting an implementation of the verkle trie in your client or prototyping/implementing some other EIP. Let them know how they can get involved with what you are working on. **AllCoreDevs in ~23h (Sept 17, 14:00 UTC)** Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/384 Stream: https://youtu.be/NorHRk5fFZU Zoom: to be share here before the call With the merge on the horizon has there been any discussions yet on the future of the different testnets? Will PoA testnets still make sense post-merge? No discussions yet AFAIK, but it's clear that new testnets will be spun up as we get close to the merge. It might make sense to actually run the merge on some of the existing execution & consensus testnets, i.e. Goerli + Prater? Wait wouldn’t testnets hardfork into eth2…? Yes, that's what I said But maybe not all? e.g. we might consider shutting Ropsten down (no more PoW needed), keeping Rinkeby as PoA, moving Goerli to a post-merge one, along with perhaps one new one (this is just me spitballing btw, none of this is "official ™️ ") <@!170317031428587520> << hah <@!552133098075193354> perhaps it would be good to conduct some survey which testnets most projects are interested in keeping surviving? I've seen various projects using various testnets, though Goerli is usually included. Yeah, that makes sense 👍 No bias 🙄 but goerli is the best If we shutdown some other testnets ChainSafe can setup a swap over our bridge to let people exchange ropsten (or other) for goerli That would be pretty trivial I think it would be worth doing a merge test with ropsten. That way we’re actually using a PoW testnet And I’d guess we’ll actually merge goerli a few times but then discard the merged chain and leave the poa one running. Easier to do that than have to setup a new eth1 chain for every merge test. wrong chain is still longest on Ropsten - `11055156`, right chain is at `11048788`

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
The second cohort of the core dev apprenticeship program is going to be kicking off in the next few weeks.  It'll run for four months during which participants will plan and execute a project focused on something in the core protocol realm.  This is your opportunity to both help these new people find a worthwhile project **and** to get more eyes and brains working on the *"thing"* that you wish more people were working on.

I encourage you to open an issue here: https://github.com/ethereum-cdap/cohort-one

It can be as simple as identifying who you are and what you are working on.  It could be an idea for a tool that seems useful.  Or maybe some data that needs to be gathered and analyzed.  Even things as ambitious as getting an implementation of the verkle trie in your client or prototyping/implementing some other EIP.  Let them know how they can get involved with what you are working on.

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: With the merge on the horizon has there been any discussions yet on the future of the different testnets?  Will PoA testnets still make sense post-merge?

excerpts.content: No discussions yet AFAIK, but it's clear that new testnets will be spun up as we get close to the merge. It might make sense to actually run the merge on some of the existing execution & consensus testnets, i.e. Goerli + Prater?
